{  
  "findings": [  
    {  
      "claim": null,  
      "finding": "Level 3 is definitional: the control rho appears directly in the measured compartment's own equation (dcq/dt) in the term alpha × rho × cq, so the quitters peak falling when rho rises follows from the model's definition, not from a paper finding.",  
      "kind": "definitional",  
      "level": 3,  
      "severity": "blocking",  
      "suggestion": "Replace the what-if with one that tests the paper's actual finding about chronic recovery, e.g. 'What if chronic recovery were fast enough to push R0 below 1?' and measure a system-wide summary such as R0 or total HCV cases, not the quitters peak.",  
      "term": "alpha × rho × cq"  
    },  
    {  
      "claim": null,  
      "finding": "Level 4 is definitional: the control eta appears directly in the measured compartment's own equation (dr/dt) in the term eta × r2 × i, so the recovered peak rising when eta rises follows from the model's definition.",  
      "kind": "definitional",  
      "level": 4,  
      "severity": "blocking",  
      "suggestion": "Replace the what-if with one that tests the paper's synergy finding, e.g. 'What if a larger share of acutely infected individuals recovered and treatment adherence were also high?' and measure R0 or total infections, not the recovered peak.",  
      "term": "eta × r2 × i"  
    },  
    {  
      "claim": null,  
      "finding": "Level 5 is definitional: the control delta appears directly in the measured compartment's own equation (dcq/dt) in the term delta × (1 − theta) × c, so the quitters peak rising when delta rises follows from the model's definition.",  
      "kind": "definitional",  
      "level": 5,  
      "severity": "blocking",  
      "suggestion": "Replace the what-if with one that tests the paper's finding on non-adherence and spread, e.g. 'What if people quit treatment half as often while adherence was high?' and measure R0 or total chronically infected individuals, not the quitters peak.",  
      "term": "delta × (1 − theta) × c"  
    },  
    {  
      "claim": {  
        "compartment": "dr/dt",  
        "parameter": "eta",  
        "says": "rate"  
      },  
      "finding": "Level 4 misdescribes the model. The words 'Acute recovery rate' and 'Speed up recovery from acute infection' treat eta as a rate, but the model identifies eta as the 'Proportion of the acutely infected who recover' (a share, not per-unit-time). The rate at which people leave the acute stage is r2.",  
      "kind": "unsupported",  
      "level": 4,  
      "severity": "blocking",  
      "suggestion": "Rename the control/title to 'Proportion of acutely infected who recover' and rephrase the what-if as 'What if a larger share of acutely infected people recovered?'"  
    ,  
      "term": null  
    },  
    {  
      "claim": null,  
      "finding": "Level 1's what-if does not teach what the level is about. The title asks 'Can adherence stop the virus?' (the paper's threshold result is R0 < 1 when θ > 0.52), but the what-if only measures the recovered peak. A higher recovered peak is not the same as stopping spread.",  
      "kind": "unsupported",  
      "level": 1,  
      "severity": "advice",  
      "suggestion": "Either rephrase the title to 'How adherence changes the recovered peak' or change the what-if to 'What if adherence exceeded the 52% threshold?' and measure R0 or total HCV infections."  
    ,  
      "term": null  
    },  
    {  
      "claim": null,  
      "finding": "Level 2's claim is worded more strongly than its measurement. The level-rule check reports the statement 'the quitters peak is higher by more than 0.006' holds on only 18 of 20 runs, so stating it as a definite outcome overstates the evidence.",  
      "kind": "unsupported",  
      "level": 2,  
      "severity": "advice",  
      "suggestion": "Reword to 'the quitters peak tends to be higher' or adjust the threshold/difference so it holds on all 20 runs, or switch the measurement to the reproduction-number contribution of β3."  
    ,  
      "term": null  
    }  
  ]  
}
